resultJson.description:
Today `Main` builds one Ember HTTP client with `TLSContext.Builder.forAsync[IO].insecure` so it can reach the Hue bridge, which serves a self-signed certificate. `SpotifyClient` and `HueClient` share that client, so every Spotify call skips certificate verification. That covers the authorize request carrying the `sp_dc` cookie, the code exchange and token renewal (client id and secret), and playback polling and tempo lookups (bearer token). Anyone who can intercept the network could pose as accounts.spotify.com or api.spotify.com and read those secrets and the playback data.

The fix gives the two clients separate TLS settings, built in a new tested factory `client.HttpClients`. `Main` is excluded from coverage, so the factory itself picks the JVM's normal trusted authorities for Spotify: the entry point `Main` calls takes no TLS argument. The bridge client keeps accepting the self-signed certificate. A second, differently named entry point lets tests trust a test certificate. That way the untrusted-certificate tests run the exact code that ships, and the trusted-certificate tests can stand up a fake Spotify over real TLS. A fake Spotify with a self-signed certificate must be rejected during the handshake, before any request bytes (body, cookie, Basic or Bearer credentials) are sent. When a call fails this way, it takes the same path as any other Spotify failure: `SyncEngine`'s poller logs `Spotify Poll Failed: <err>` at ERROR and polls again on the next interval. Retry, backoff and logging behaviour stay as they are, and no config switch is added.

The work is done when all of these hold:
- Spotify calls are verified.
- Bridge setup, area listing and streaming still work end to end through `Main` against a self-signed bridge.
- Every acceptance criterion has a test, using real TLS sockets where the criterion is about TLS.
- The docs no longer list disabled Spotify certificate checks as a known limitation, and the roadmap item is gone.

Some tests cannot fail before the change; they are regression guards. These are the bridge and trusted-Spotify tests (criteria 3 and 4), apart from not compiling without `HttpClients`. They catch an over-broad fix, such as verifying the bridge too or breaking Spotify over TLS. The tests that do fail on the old code are the untrusted-certificate tests (criteria 1 and 2) and the docs test (criterion 5).

tasks.title: Give Spotify a certificate-verifying HTTP client and the bridge its own self-signed-accepting client
tasks.description:
Add `src/main/scala/client/HttpClients.scala` with `package client` and brace syntax, containing `final case class HttpClients[F[_]](spotify: Client[F], bridge: Client[F])` and its companion `object HttpClients`:
- `def resource[F[_]: Async: Network]: Resource[F, HttpClients[F]]` is what Main uses. It builds the system TLS context itself, e.g. `Resource.eval(Network[F].tlsContext.system).flatMap(trusting)`. Alternatively it builds the Spotify client with `EmberClientBuilder.default[F].build` and no `withTLSContext`, because Ember then falls back to the system context. Either way, `Main` passes no trust setting.
- `def trusting[F[_]: Async: Network](trusted: TLSContext[F]): Resource[F, HttpClients[F]]` lets tests trust a test certificate. It needs a different name because Scalafix's `SameParamOverloading` lint is an error.
- Spotify client: Ember with `.withTLSContext(trusted)`. Leave endpoint identification on (Ember's default) and keep the `FollowRedirect(2)` wrapping as today.
- Bridge client: Ember with `Network[F].tlsContext.insecure`, also wrapped in `FollowRedirect(2)`, so bridge traffic behaves exactly as it does now. Add a one-line scaladoc saying the bridge serves a self-signed certificate.

In `Main.start`, replace the `tlsContext`/`httpClient` lines (32-33) with `clients <- HttpClients.resource[IO]`. Pass `clients.spotify` to `SpotifyClient.resource` and `clients.bridge` to `new HueClient`, and drop the imports that are no longer used (`TLSContext`, and possibly `EmberClientBuilder` and `FollowRedirect`). Change nothing else in Main.

Test fixtures:
- Commit a self-signed PKCS12 keystore at `src/test/resources/self-signed.p12`, e.g. `keytool -genkeypair -alias fake -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 36500 -dname CN=localhost -ext SAN=dns:localhost,ip:127.0.0.1 -storetype PKCS12 -storepass changeit -keypass changeit -keystore src/test/resources/self-signed.p12`.
- Add `src/test/scala/testkit/Tls.scala` (`package testkit`, `object Tls`; the DirectoryAndPackageName and FileNameConsistent lints require these names) with these helpers:
  - `selfSigned: IO[TLSContext[IO]]`, which is `Network[IO].tlsContext.fromKeyStoreResource("self-signed.p12", pw, pw)`. It serves as both the fake server's identity and a trust store that trusts it.
  - `server(app: HttpApp[IO]): Resource[IO, (Int, IO[List[Request[IO]]])]`: an Ember server with `.withTLS(selfSigned)`, host 127.0.0.1 and port 0. It records every request that reaches the app, with the method, path and headers available.
  - `redirectTo(port: Int)(client: Client[IO]): Client[IO]`: a middleware that rewrites only the request authority to `localhost:<port>` (always `localhost`, never an IP) and keeps `https`. The hard-coded `accounts.spotify.com`/`api.spotify.com` URIs then reach the fake, and its certificate is still checked against the `localhost` host name.

Add `src/test/scala/client/HttpClientsSpec.scala` (CatsEffectSuite) with three tests:
- A GET through `HttpClients.resource[IO]`'s `spotify` to the self-signed server fails with an `javax.net.ssl.SSLException` somewhere in the cause chain, and the server records no requests. This test fails on the old insecure client.
- The same GET through `HttpClients.trusting(selfSigned)`'s `spotify` succeeds.
- `HttpClients.resource[IO]`'s `bridge` gets a 200 from the self-signed server.

Don't add a HueClient-over-bridge test or log-absence checks here; Task 3 covers the bridge end to end.

tasks.title: Show Spotify calls fail on an untrusted certificate without sending anything, polling logs it and carries on, and trusted TLS still works
tasks.description:
Add `src/test/scala/client/SpotifyTlsSpec.scala` (`package client`, CatsEffectSuite). Build clients as `new SpotifyClient[IO](Tls.redirectTo(port)(clients.spotify), SpotifyCredentials("id", "secret", "refresh"), session, deferred)`, with `clients` from `HttpClients.resource[IO]` for the untrusted cases and `HttpClients.trusting(selfSigned)` for the trusted ones. The fake Spotify is a `Tls.server` with routes like SpotifyClientSpec's: `GET /authorize`, `POST /api/token`, `GET /v1/me/player` and `GET /v1/audio-features/<id>`.

Untrusted case (production `resource`). These fail on the old code. Each call fails with an `SSLException` in the cause chain, and the fake records no request:
- With session `Some`, `getPlaybackState` and `getTempo` fail, so no bearer token is sent.
- With session `None`, `getPlaybackState` triggers sign-in and fails on the authorize GET. The fake records neither the authorize request (with its `sp_dc` cookie) nor any `POST /api/token`, so neither the cookie nor the client secret is sent. Add a timeout so a regression can't hang on `authCodeDeferred.get`.
- Call `renew` directly. `SpotifySession` has no expiry and renewal only happens after a 401, so going through a poll would never reach it. The fake must record no `POST /api/token`.

Trusted case (`trusting(selfSigned)`). These are regression guards, not fail-first tests; the existing SpotifyClientSpec already covers the logic.
- Sign-in: the fake's `GET /authorize` completes the deferred with a code, `POST /api/token` exchanges it (`grant_type=authorization_code`), and `getPlaybackState` then succeeds with the new bearer token.
- One bearer call over TLS: the player rejects the first token with a 401, a single renewal follows, and the poll succeeds; then `getTempo` returns the BPM. Reuse the token and playing JSON from SpotifyClientSpec.

Engine case (fails on the old code). Run `SyncEngine.make(...).run` with the untrusted Spotify client, a fake `Lights` and an AppConfig like SyncEngineRunSpec's, with `pollingIntervalMs = 100`. Use real time, because TestControl can't drive sockets. Wrap the client in a counting middleware placed outside `redirectTo`, and take frames for about 1–2 seconds with `interruptAfter`. Assert all of the following:
- The stream completes without error.
- More than one poll attempt was counted.
- Captured logs contain an ERROR from the `SyncEngine` logger whose message has `Spotify Poll Failed` and the TLS cause (`SSLHandshakeException`, `PKIX` or `certificate`). Asserting that this line is present is safe even though the ROOT logger is shared with suites running in parallel. Don't assert that any log is absent.

First check what Ember actually raises. If the logged `$err` toString doesn't show the TLS cause, for example because Ember wraps the exception, make the smallest change at that log line in `SyncEngine.run` so the cause shows. Otherwise leave main code alone.

tasks.title: End-to-end: the app starts, lists areas and starts streaming on a self-signed Hue bridge
tasks.description:
Add a test to `src/test/scala/MainSpec.scala` (no package, like the rest of the file). It runs a fake bridge as `Tls.server` with the self-signed keystore. The fake serves:
- `GET /clip/v2/resource/entertainment_configuration` with one music area that has channels
- `GET .../entertainment` and `GET .../room`
- `GET .../entertainment_configuration/<id>`, returning `data[0].channels` with `channel_id`s
- `PUT .../entertainment_configuration/<id>`, recording the `action` from the JSON body

Reuse the JSON shapes from HueClientSpec.

Start `Main.start` with a HOCON source built like MainSpec's `hocon`/`source` (falling back to `reference.conf`, so `beat-source` stays `spotify` and no audio device is opened). Set:
- `hue.creds.address = "127.0.0.1:<port>"` and a valid PSK
- `ui.enabled = false`
- `polling-interval-ms = 3600000`. `Stream.awakeEvery` waits a full interval before the first poll, and `getTempo` only runs once something is playing, so the test never contacts Spotify. Without this, the poller would sign in and send a real GET to accounts.spotify.com with the developer's `SPOTIFY_SP_DC` cookie.

Run it under `.timeout(a few seconds).attempt`. Assert positively on bridge traffic: the fake recorded the three list GETs, the zone GET and a PUT with `action = start`, which `EntertainmentStream.toBridge` sends on the first frame. Don't assert that certificate errors are absent from the log. The ROOT appender also catches log lines from other suites running in parallel, including the deliberate TLS failures in SpotifyTlsSpec, so absence checks are flaky. The positive bridge checks already show the bridge's self-signed certificate was accepted. Main also binds the callback server on 127.0.0.1:7070, as the existing MainSpec start tests do. The DTLS connection to 127.0.0.1:2100 will fail after the PUT; that's expected and isn't asserted on.

This is a regression guard: it passes on the old code, and it fails if the fix also turns on verification for the bridge or hands `Main`'s `HueClient` the Spotify client.

tasks.title: Remove the certificate limitation from the docs and the roadmap
tasks.description:
Make these doc changes:
- `docs/how-it-works.md`: delete the `Certificate checks are off.` bullet in `## Known limitations` (line 372).
- `docs/roadmap.md`: delete the `Keep certificate checks on for Spotify.` item (line 7). It is the only item under `## Fixes`, so remove that heading too.
- `docs/architecture.md`, line 273 in the Startup sequence diagram: change `M->>S: build HTTP client and start callback server on :7070` to say Main builds two HTTP clients. Spotify's checks certificates; the bridge's accepts its self-signed certificate.

Add `src/test/scala/DocsSpec.scala` (munit FunSuite, no package, `object`-free test class `DocsSpec`). It reads the doc files relative to the project root, as `DocImages` does with `Paths.get("docs", ...)`, because sbt runs tests from the root. Two tests:
- Extract the `## Known limitations` section of `docs/how-it-works.md` up to the next `## ` heading, and assert that no line mentions both Spotify and certificate verification or checks.
- Assert that `docs/roadmap.md` has no `Keep certificate checks on for Spotify` item.

Both fail on the current docs.

resultJson.brief:
Project: a Scala 3 app (sbt, root at /work/spotify-hue-sync) that syncs Hue lights to Spotify playback. Read CLAUDE.md first.

Conventions:
- Brace syntax; `given`/`using`/`summon`, never `implicit`.
- Cats Effect `F[_]: Async`, `Resource`, `Ref`. No Future, no threads, no unsafeRun outside Main.
- Errors are raised in F.
- Make the smallest change at the problem and don't reshape working code. Comment only what the code can't say.
- Tests use munit with `CatsEffectSuite`. No comments in tests; the test name says what it checks.
- Use `TestControl` for timed code. It can't drive real sockets, so TLS tests use real time, short intervals and `.timeout`.

Done means:
- Run `sbt fix`, then `sbt check`. It lints with Scalafix (`.scalafix.conf` for main, `.scalafix.test.conf` for tests), then tests with coverage. The minimums are ≥90% statements and ≥85% branches overall, and ≥70% statements per file.
- Never lower the minimums or widen `coverageExcludedPackages` (currently `Main;audio.AudioCapture;client.DtlsEmitter;beat.BeatTracking`). So the new `client/HttpClients.scala` must be covered by tests.
- Scalafix lints that fail the build:
  - `DirectoryAndPackageName`: the package must match the directory, e.g. `package testkit` for `src/test/scala/testkit/Tls.scala`, `package client` for `client/`, and no package at the test root.
  - `FileNameConsistent`: the file name matches its top-level definition.
  - `SameParamOverloading`: don't overload a method with the same parameter shapes; use distinct names.
  - `ObjectFinal`, `Implicit`, `CatsImplicitsImport`.
- Never read, print or commit `.env`.

Build: `build.sbt` sets neither `fork` nor `parallelExecution`, so test suites run in parallel in one JVM and share the logback ROOT logger. A log-capturing `ListAppender` sees lines from other suites. Only assert that specific lines are present, filtered by logger name if possible, never that lines are absent.

Key files:
- `src/main/scala/Main.scala`: `Main.start(source: ConfigSource): IO[ExitCode]` builds the app as one Resource. Lines 32-33 are the problem: `tlsContext <- Resource.eval(TLSContext.Builder.forAsync[IO].insecure)` and `httpClient <- EmberClientBuilder.default[IO].withTLSContext(tlsContext).build.map { c => FollowRedirect(2)(c) }`. Line 35 is `SpotifyClient.resource[IO](httpClient, config.spotify)` (it binds the callback server on 127.0.0.1:7070) and line 36 is `new HueClient[IO](config.hue.creds, httpClient)`. Then come `Lights.fromBridge`, `lights.areas`, `MusicArea.choose`, `hueClient.getChannels(area.id)` and `SyncEngine.make`. `engine.run.through(EntertainmentStream.toBridge(hueClient, emitter))` sends `setStreaming(area, true)` on the first frame, then opens DTLS to bridge:2100. Main is excluded from coverage, but MainSpec runs `Main.start` directly.
- `src/main/scala/client/SpotifyClient.scala`: `class SpotifyClient[F[_]: Async: Network](client: Client[F], creds: SpotifyCredentials, session: Ref[F, Option[SpotifySession]], authCodeDeferred: Deferred[F, String])`. It uses colon/indent style; leave that as is.
  - The hosts are hard-coded:
    - `GET https://accounts.spotify.com/authorize?...` with header `Cookie: sp_dc=${sys.env SPOTIFY_SP_DC}`.
    - `POST https://accounts.spotify.com/api/token` with Basic client id/secret. It is used for the code exchange in `initialAuth` and in `renew: F[String]`, which is public.
    - `GET https://api.spotify.com/v1/me/player` (`getPlaybackState: F[Option[PlaybackState]]`) and `/v1/audio-features/<id>` (`getTempo(id: TrackId): F[Option[Double]]`), both through `authorised`, which sends a Bearer token and renews once on a 401.
  - `getOrRefresh` calls `initialAuth` when the session is None. `initialAuth` blocks on `authCodeDeferred.get` after the authorize GET.
  - `SpotifySession(accessToken, refreshToken)` has no expiry.
  - Test against the hard-coded hosts by wrapping the real Ember client in a middleware that rewrites only the authority to `localhost:<port>`, keeping https and the host name `localhost`. Don't change SpotifyClient.
- `src/main/scala/client/HueClient.scala`: `new HueClient[F](creds: HueCredentials, httpClient: Client[F])`, base `https://${creds.address}/clip/v2`, where the address may include a port.
  - `getChannels(zoneId)`: GET `resource/entertainment_configuration/<id>`; reads `data[0].channels[].channel_id`.
  - `areas`: GETs `resource/entertainment_configuration`, `resource/entertainment` and `resource/room`.
  - `setStreaming(zoneId, active)`: PUT with `{"action":"start"|"stop"}`.
  - Errors are `HueApiError`.
- `src/main/scala/SyncEngine.scala`:
  - The poller (line 112): `Stream.awakeEvery[F](config.pollingIntervalMs.millis).evalMap(_ => spotify.getPlaybackState.handleErrorWith { err => logger.error(s"Spotify Poll Failed: $err") *> Async[F].pure(None) })`. The first poll comes only after one full interval.
  - `getTempo` is only called when a track is playing, and logs a WARN on failure.
  - `SyncEngine.make[IO](config: AppConfig, live, spotify, zone, lights, random, audio)`. `run: Stream[F, Frame]` emits paused frames even without playback.
- `src/main/scala/domain/config/AppConfig.scala`: `AppConfig(spotify, hue, pollingIntervalMs: Int = 2000, lightShow, ui)`. Nothing validates `pollingIntervalMs`, and its HOCON key is `polling-interval-ms`. `reference.conf` defaults `light-show.beat-source = "spotify"` and `ui.enabled = true`. `application.conf` sets audio, so MainSpec-style sources fall back to `reference.conf` only.
- Test patterns to copy:
  - `src/test/scala/client/SpotifyClientSpec.scala`: fake Spotify routes, the token JSON `{ "access_token", "token_type", "expires_in", "scope", "refresh_token"? }`, the playing JSON, and the `expiring`/`renewedTo` helpers.
  - `src/test/scala/client/HueClientSpec.scala`: bridge JSON for areas, channels and streaming.
  - `src/test/scala/SyncEngineRunSpec.scala`: the AppConfig, fake `Lights` and `LiveSettings.make` setup.
  - `src/test/scala/MainSpec.scala`: the `hocon`/`source` config builders and the `capturedLogs` ListAppender on ROOT.
- Docs:
  - `docs/how-it-works.md:372`: the Known limitations bullet.
  - `docs/roadmap.md:7`: the only item under `## Fixes`.
  - `docs/architecture.md:273`: the startup sequence diagram line.
  - `DocImages` reads `Paths.get("docs", ...)` relative to the project root.

http4s/fs2 notes (http4s 0.23.33, fs2 3.12.2, CE 3.6.3):
- `Network[F].tlsContext` (also `TLSContext.Builder.forAsync[F]`) offers `.system: F[TLSContext[F]]`, `.insecure` and `.fromKeyStoreResource(name, storePassword, keyPassword)`. `fromKeyStore*` uses the keystore for both key managers and trust managers, so one self-signed p12 serves as the fake server's identity and as the test trust store.
- `EmberClientBuilder.default[F].withTLSContext(ctx).build`. Without `withTLSContext`, Ember uses the system context. Endpoint identification is on by default, so the test cert needs SAN `dns:localhost`, and the redirect must target `localhost`.
- `EmberServerBuilder.default[F].withTLS(ctx).withHost(ipv4"127.0.0.1").withPort(port"0")`. Read the bound port from `server.address.getPort`. The Ember server may log failed handshakes; that's expected.
- A certificate failure surfaces as `javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException`, often with "PKIX path building failed", and Ember may wrap it, so match on the cause chain. The handshake fails before any HTTP bytes are written, so a request-recording fake server with no recorded requests proves that no body, cookie or credentials were sent.
- The test keystore is test-only, so a fixed password such as `changeit` is fine. Generate it with JDK keytool, with SANs for localhost and 127.0.0.1 and a validity of about 100 years.
